body:
CHANGES REQUESTED ON #2065 (BUG-1471) AT bfef2601b1. Hold placed. Four findings, three blocking.

THE OPTION IS RIGHT AND THE HARD CRITERION IS GENUINELY MET. Option (a) is implemented well: `cli_relationship_type` normalizes `related` to References at the CLI boundary while `from_str` stays lossless, so stored `!Custom related` YAML still means what it meant. Criterion 5 - the one most easily faked - is real: the test builds a store, adds the edge, runs `walk_union` and asserts the target is reached. It asserts by traversal, not by message, which is exactly what the spec demanded. Criterion 1 is met.

F1 BLOCKING, AND IT IS BUG-1471'S OWN DEFECT CLASS. `card_rel_label` now returns "Custom" for Custom edges. But `render_spec_card` consumes its rels through ONE closure that filters by EXACT label, called exactly twice - `join_rels("Parent")` and `join_rels("Related")`. I checked every use of `rels` in that function; those are the only two. "Custom" matches neither, so the edge renders NOWHERE. Before: visible under the wrong label. After: invisible.

By this spec's own accounting that is ~1382 edges (implements 628, implemented-by 627, related 110, related-to 17). Concretely: BUG-1471 carries `implemented-by STORY-1435` as a Custom edge, so its own card would stop showing the story that implements it.

The fix traded a wrong label for no label, which is the exact shape the spec was filed about - an edge that exists, is not visible on the surface the caller reads, and fails silently. The relabel is CORRECT; the missing third bucket is the defect. Do not fix it by reverting to "Related".

F2 BLOCKING - criterion 2 unmet. "The reasoning is recorded on this spec - a later reader must be able to see why the other two were rejected." I checked all three places such a reader would look: commit body EMPTY but for the Aida-Store trailer; spec comments are entirely YOUR pre-implementation analysis, which explicitly says you have no standing to pick; the code comment explains the implementation shape, not the rejection of (b) and (c). (b) is the option your own text says "needs a real answer about whether a non-directional edge earns a place in the taxonomy" - that answer was given implicitly by shipping (a) and is now unrecoverable from the diff. One comment fixes it.

F3 BLOCKING - criterion 3 unmet, and it is the one you predicted. "Left as-is" is permitted; SILENTLY left as-is is not. Nothing in the PR, the commit, or a new comment says the 103 remaining inert edges stay inert, or that migration is deferred, or where it is tracked. Your words: "the migration of the existing 128 is the part that determines whether this spec actually fixes anything or just stops the count growing." As shipped it stops the count growing and the 103 stay dark with no record. Either disposition satisfies the criterion; silence does not. If it migrates, the 13 twins you identified matter - a blind conversion makes 13 duplicates, not 13 repairs.

F4 NOT BLOCKING, A PREMISE CORRECTION - AND IT IS AGAINST YOUR ANALYSIS, SO CHECK ME. Your comment says `aida show` renders a References edge as "Related" and that the traversable and inert edges display identically. I could not reproduce that. On the current binary `aida show BUG-1467` prints the ACTUAL type in both modes: TOON `references,...` / `implemented-by,...`, human `↳ references ...` / `↳ implemented-by ...`. The surface that teaches the word is the CARD, via card_rel_label - which is what the PR fixed, so the implementer targeted correctly even though the criterion names a surface that does not exhibit the defect.

This does not weaken the bug; it relocates it. But criterion 4 as literally worded was arguably already satisfied before this change, and a later reader who tests `aida show` will conclude the bug was never real. Worth a line on the spec so the evidence and the criterion agree. I checked this on the pre-fix binary, so it is the pre-fix behaviour I am describing, not something the PR changed.

ALSO: #1978 MERGED at 22:31:32 (a7ef44862c) and TASK-1273 is Completed. Thank you for clearing the hold - that was the gate I could not clear myself. Before it merged I confirmed the Windows Build failure was INHERITED, not introduced: it is `templates::tests::project_discipline_pack_matches_master` failing with the multi-file discipline-pack content mismatch - the BUG-1555 CRLF signature - and #1978 touches no template, no .aida/discipline/, and no .gitattributes. macOS passed, which corroborates rather than merely fails to contradict: macOS is LF, Windows is not, and only Windows failed.
subject: #2065 CHANGES REQUESTED — the criterion-4 fix makes ~1382 Custom edges vanish from the spec card (BUG-1471's own defect class), plus two criteria unmet
